solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The majority long to adopt high-class facial growth

indicators.note: to adopt something is to take it in, so one piece takes another inside itself

blocks.note: the majority is most of something
U is the old British label for upper-class usage
to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: Most people would like to grow a posh-looking beard or moustache.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside MOST, then ACHE follows. U (upper-class) is a crossword staple from the old U and non-U distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: A moustache is hair grown on the upper lip, the classic example of growth on a face.

clue.text: Beginning of month — occasion for seafaring?

blocks.note: the first day of March can be written MAR I, with I as the Roman numeral one, which begins that month
an occasion is a time, as in 'the last time we met'

explanation.surface: Is the start of the month a good moment for a sea voyage?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading of the start of a month as the date 'Mar I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime describes things connected with the sea, so it means relating to or used for seafaring.

clue.text: Vessel originally used by navy

indicators.note: originally points to the origin, the very start, of the word beside it

blocks.note: the opening letter of used
RN stands for the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A pot once employed by the fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a container such as a vase, and vessel is a general word for any container.

clue.text: Jog round university to find fish

indicators.note: round means placed around, so one word surrounds another

blocks.note: to jog is to trot, running at a gentle pace
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A runner circles the campus looking for a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The trout is a common freshwater fish related to salmon, so it is an example of a fish.

clue.text: Woman involved in scam, running into stars

indicators.note: running suggests letters set in motion and rearranged rather than staying put
something involved in a thing sits within it, so one piece goes inside the others

blocks.note: a con is a swindle
Stella is a woman's name
the letters of into rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman caught up in a fraud ends up seeing stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' feels like a verb or a celebrity reading, but it is the definition; fittingly, Stella is Latin for star.
explanation.definitionFit: A constellation is a named group of stars, so the plural noun stars stands for it.

clue.text: Oriental seabird overwhelmed by raging sea

indicators.note: a raging sea is wild and churned up, so its letters are tossed into a new order
in a down entry, being overwhelmed means sitting under the other piece, so it is written after it

blocks.note: the letters of sea rearranged
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A bird from the East is swamped by stormy waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and eastern are synonyms, both describing things from the East, especially Asia.

clue.text: Delight in archaeological excavation

blocks.note: first meaning: to like or enjoy, in slang
second meaning: a site being dug by archaeologists

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an archaeologist's joy at finding something; the slang verb 'to dig' means to enjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: The short word is slang for enjoying something and also the ordinary noun for a site being excavated.

clue.text: Lower your, and my, carriage

blocks.note: to demean is to lower in dignity
belonging to you and me together

explanation.surface: An instruction to lower a vehicle belonging to you and me.
explanation.walkthrough: Carriage is not a vehicle here but the way one holds oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage means bearing or deportment, and demeanour is outward behaviour and bearing.

clue.text: Vigorously attack bearded mammal

blocks.note: first meaning: read as two words
second meaning: a farm animal with a tuft of chin hair

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning splits the answer into the phrase 'go at', to set about something energetically.
explanation.definitionFit: A goat is a horned farm animal, the billy famous for its beard, and 'go at' means to attack.

clue.text: Managed to proceed, reaching Burmese city

blocks.note: to manage a business is to run it
to proceed is to go on

explanation.surface: Someone managed to keep travelling until they arrived in Myanmar's largest city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangoon is the former name of Yangon, long the capital of Burma, now Myanmar.

clue.text: Man or woman backing sailor's dance

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: Sam can be short for Samuel or Samantha
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: Someone supports a seaman's dance routine.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is a lively Brazilian dance, so it is an example of a dance.

clue.text: It's a principle, whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: reading from either end gives the same result, which is what a word spelt identically both ways does

blocks.note: a core belief, a word that reads the same in both directions

explanation.surface: A rule that holds true however you view it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a principle being universally true; the phrase is really saying the word reads identically both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a belief or doctrine held as true, so it is a principle.

clue.text: Yearning for past? In Angola it's unusual

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are set out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Pining for the old days is rare in Angola.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like part of the fodder but is only a link; the nine letters come from 'Angola it's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a sentimental longing for times gone by, which a yearning for the past describes.

clue.text: Old citizen's article connected with prohibition

blocks.note: the definite article
a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: An elderly resident has an item about a ban.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A Theban was an inhabitant of Thebes, the ancient Greek or Egyptian city, so an old citizen.

clue.text: One lambasted for keeping old cut off

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to slate is to criticise harshly
O is a common abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A person is attacked for hanging on to outdated things.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut off as an adjective means separated or remote, which is what isolated means.

clue.text: Assorted male cousins unexpectedly entertaining the Spanish

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning up in a surprising order
a host entertaining a guest has them inside, so one piece is taken in

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A mixed bunch of male relatives surprise everyone by hosting Spanish visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Assorted means of various kinds mixed together, a synonym for miscellaneous.

clue.text: Former player, one making extortionate demands

blocks.note: ex means former
a player in a theatre is an actor

explanation.surface: A retired performer turned out to be a blackmailer.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to demand and obtain forcibly, so an exactor is a person who extorts.

clue.text: Criticise a close relative's headgear

blocks.note: critics pan a show they dislike
taken as written
ma is a mother

explanation.surface: A dig at a family member's choice of hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A panama is a lightweight straw hat, so it is a kind of headgear.

clue.text: Danger originally preventing return of old Italian currency

indicators.note: originally points to the origin, the first letter, of the word beside it
a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: the opening letter of preventing
Italy used the lira, plural lire, before the euro

explanation.surface: A risk that first stops Italy going back to its old money.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril means serious danger, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: In Pennsylvania, a way to serve lasagne, say

indicators.note: in places the following words inside the abbreviated state name

blocks.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
taken as written
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A Pennsylvania method of serving lasagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks lasagne as one example of the category.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is one type of Italian pasta, so the definition gives an example of the answer.

clue.text: Considered a suitable material for hats

blocks.note: first meaning: thought or believed, past tense of feel
second meaning: a matted woollen fabric

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one judgement about a fabric, but considered is a separate past-tense verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt is the past tense of feel, to believe, and also the pressed wool cloth used for trilbies and fedoras.

clue.text: Rowing crew had a meal, some would say

indicators.note: what people would say refers to how words are pronounced rather than written

blocks.note: past tense of eat, pronounced like the number by many speakers

explanation.surface: The rowers ate together, people report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some would say' hedges because many British speakers pronounce ate as 'et'.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing boat with eight oarsmen, and its crew, is called an eight.

clue.text: Sort of coffee popular fellow initially took

indicators.note: initially signals the starting letter of the word it accompanies

blocks.note: something popular is in
Stan is a man's name, a fellow
the opening letter of took

explanation.surface: A well-liked man was the first to grab a type of coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Instant coffee is made from soluble powder, so instant names a sort of coffee.

clue.text: Seek information in capacity of king

blocks.note: as means in the role of, as in 'acting as'
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone makes enquiries while acting as monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask is to put a question, which is how one seeks information.

clue.text: Sporting group fails to finish meal

indicators.note: failing to finish means stopping short, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: A sports side doesn't complete its dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea in Britain is also a light afternoon meal or an evening meal, not just the drink.

clue.text: Plundered and beat it, getting fired

blocks.note: to beat it is to run away
to be fired from a job is to be sacked

explanation.surface: A worker looted the place, fled and lost their job.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack is to search thoroughly and rob, so ransacked means plundered.
